On a successful request, the AesGcmDecryptor shall decrypt the buffer in place and emit the plaintext on `decryptOut` with status `SUCCESS`.
Requirement.rationale: Plaintext is never longer than ciphertext, so no second buffer is needed.

Requirement.text: The AesGcmDecryptor shall authenticate, as AES-GCM AAD, the masked TC primary header carrying the virtual channel ID together with the SA index, and reject a frame authenticated for any other VC or SA.
Requirement.rationale: CCSDS 355.0-B-2 binds a frame to its VC and SA.

Requirement.text: The AesGcmDecryptor shall return `MAC_VERIFICATION_FAILURE`, distinct from `DECRYPTION_FAILURE`, when the IV, ciphertext, or MAC has been modified or the frame was not built for this SA and VC, and shall remain able to decrypt subsequent frames.
Requirement.rationale: CCSDS 355.0-B-2 sect. 3.3.3.2 requires an authentication verdict distinguishable from a processing error; the two call for different ground responses.

Requirement.text: The AesGcmDecryptor shall return `DECRYPTION_FAILURE`, without requesting a key, for a buffer too short to hold an IV and a MAC.
Requirement.rationale: An uplink buffer is attacker-influenced and must be bounded before use; the ciphertext length is handed to OpenSSL as an `int`.

Requirement.text: The AesGcmDecryptor shall return `KEY_ERROR` when the key manager reports failure or supplies a key that is not AES-256 sized.
Requirement.rationale: A wrong-sized key would otherwise decrypt under unintended material.

Requirement.text: The buffer emitted on `decryptOut` shall retain the allocation context and original allocation pointer of the buffer received on `decryptIn`.
Requirement.rationale: `Svc.BufferManager` deallocates by context and asserts the data pointer lies within the slot it issued.

Requirement.text: A buffer received on `decryptReturnIn` shall be returned on `bufferReturnOut`.
Requirement.rationale: Every buffer emitted is the one that arrived.

Requirement.text: On a successful request, the AesGcmEncryptor shall emit on `encryptOut` a buffer laid out as IV (12) \
Requirement.rationale: ciphertext \

Requirement.text: The AesGcmEncryptor shall authenticate, as AES-GCM AAD, the masked TM primary header carrying the virtual channel ID together with the SA index.
Requirement.rationale: CCSDS 355.0-B-2 binds a frame to its VC and SA.

Requirement.text: The AesGcmEncryptor shall draw a fresh IV from the CSPRNG for every frame.
Requirement.rationale: A repeated IV under one key forfeits GCM's confidentiality and authenticity.

Requirement.text: The AesGcmEncryptor shall return `KEY_ERROR` when the key manager reports failure or supplies a key that is not AES-256 sized.
Requirement.rationale: A wrong-sized key would otherwise encrypt under unintended material.

Requirement.text: The AesGcmEncryptor shall return `ENCRYPTION_FAILURE` when the plaintext plus IV and MAC would exceed the TM data field less the 2-byte SA index (`ComCfg.TmFrameFixedSize` - 6 - 2 - 2).
Requirement.rationale: A larger output would overrun the transfer frame data field in `Svc.Ccsds.TmFramer`.

Requirement.text: The AesGcmEncryptor shall return the incoming plaintext buffer on `bufferReturnOut`, unmodified.
Requirement.rationale: The plaintext belongs to its sender and is not encrypted in place.

Requirement.text: The AesGcmEncryptor shall mark its output store available again when the emitted buffer arrives on `encryptReturnIn`.
Requirement.rationale: The store is component memory, not allocator memory.

Requirement.text: The AesGcmEncryptor shall authenticate, in the AAD, the virtual channel ID carried on the frame context.
Requirement.rationale: The TM primary header does not exist at encryption time; the context carries the VC that `Svc::Ccsds::TmFramer` will write into it.

Requirement.text: The AesGcmEncryptor shall drop a frame with `ENCRYPTION_FAILURE` and the `OutputBufferBusy` event, rather than overwrite its output store, when a previously emitted frame has not yet returned on `encryptReturnIn`.
Requirement.rationale: The store is a single buffer; overwriting it would let the new frame's MAC cover a silent substitution.

Requirement.text: The AesGcmEncryptor shall emit on `encryptOut` only its own output store, and shall return the incoming plaintext on `bufferReturnOut` on every path, with a failed frame reporting its status against an empty buffer.
Requirement.rationale: Keeps buffer ownership unambiguous on the return path.

Requirement.text: The AesGcmEncryptor shall return `ENCRYPTION_FAILURE` rather than emit a frame if the CSPRNG cannot supply an IV.
Requirement.rationale: Encrypting under a stale or predictable IV is worse than dropping the frame.

Requirement.text: The CcsdsSdlsDeframer shall accept framed SDLS data with frame context via the `Svc.Deframer` interface (guarded `dataIn`).
Requirement.rationale: Standard deframing pipeline entry point.

Requirement.text: Upon receiving a frame containing at least 16 bits, the CcsdsSdlsDeframer shall extract the leading 16-bit security association (SA) index and record it in the frame context (`saIndex`).
Requirement.rationale: The SA index selects the decryption path and must accompany the data.

Requirement.text: The CcsdsSdlsDeframer shall remove the SA index from the frame and pass the remaining data, the SA index, and the updated context to the decryption helper via `decryptOut`.
Requirement.rationale: The decryption helper operates on the iv/data, not the SA header.

Requirement.text: Upon receiving a frame shorter than 16 bits, the CcsdsSdlsDeframer shall emit the `InsufficientLength` WARNING_HI event, shall not invoke the decryption helper, and shall return the frame buffer via `dataReturnOut`.
Requirement.rationale: Malformed input must be reported and its buffer must not leak.

Requirement.text: Upon a non-SUCCESS status passed forward on `decryptIn`, the CcsdsSdlsDeframer shall emit the `DecryptionFailed` WARNING_HI event, notify `errorNotify` with `SDLS_DECRYPTION_FAILURE`, and return ownership of the accompanying buffer to the decryption subsystem via `decryptReturnOut`.
Requirement.rationale: Decryption failures must be visible to the system and the buffer must not leak.

Requirement.text: The CcsdsSdlsDeframer shall pass successfully decrypted data received on `decryptIn` downstream via `dataOut`.
Requirement.rationale: Continues the deframing pipeline with plaintext data.

Requirement.text: The CcsdsSdlsDeframer shall route ownership returns of downstream data (`dataReturnIn`) to the decryption helper via `decryptReturnOut`.
Requirement.rationale: Decrypted buffers are owned by the decryption subsystem.

Requirement.text: The CcsdsSdlsDeframer shall return iv/data buffers received back from the decryption helper (`bufferReturnIn`) upstream via `dataReturnOut`.
Requirement.rationale: Original frame buffers must return to their upstream allocator.

Requirement.text: The CcsdsSdlsFramer shall accept data with frame context via the `Svc.Framer` interface (`dataIn`).
Requirement.rationale: Standard framing pipeline entry point.

Requirement.text: The CcsdsSdlsFramer shall determine the security association (SA) index from the frame context when set, otherwise from the `SA_INDEX` parameter, record it in the frame context, and pass the data, SA index, and context to the encryption helper via `encryptOut`.
Requirement.rationale: The SA index selects the encryption path; upstream components may override the configured default.

Requirement.text: Upon receiving encrypted data on `encryptIn`, the CcsdsSdlsFramer shall allocate a frame buffer via `bufferAllocate`, prepend the 16-bit SA index to the encrypted data, return ownership of the encrypted buffer via `encryptReturnOut`, and pass the resulting SDLS frame downstream via `dataOut`.
Requirement.rationale: The SA index must lead the frame so the receiving deframer can extract it; prepending requires a new allocation.

Requirement.text: Upon a non-SUCCESS status passed forward on `encryptIn`, the CcsdsSdlsFramer shall emit the `EncryptionFailed` WARNING_HI event subject to its throttle and return ownership of the accompanying buffer to the encryption subsystem via `encryptReturnOut`, and emit a ready-for-more com status on `comStatusOut`.
Requirement.rationale: Encryption failures must be visible to the system, the buffer must not leak, and a ComQueue-driven downlink must not stall.

Requirement.text: The CcsdsSdlsFramer shall deallocate frame buffers received back on `dataReturnIn` via `bufferDeallocate`.
Requirement.rationale: The framer allocated the frame buffer and must release it.

Requirement.text: The CcsdsSdlsFramer shall return original data buffers received back from the encryption helper (`bufferReturnIn`) upstream via `dataReturnOut`.
Requirement.rationale: Original data buffers must return to their upstream allocator.

Requirement.text: The CcsdsSdlsFramer shall pass com status received on `comStatusIn` through to `comStatusOut` unmodified.
Requirement.rationale: Ready signals must traverse the framing pipeline.

Requirement.text: Upon an invalid or undersized buffer allocation, the CcsdsSdlsFramer shall emit the `BufferAllocationFailed` WARNING_HI event subject to its throttle, deallocate the undersized buffer when valid, return the encrypted buffer via `encryptReturnOut`, and emit a ready-for-more com status on `comStatusOut`.
Requirement.rationale: Allocation failures must be reported, no buffer may leak, and a ComQueue-driven downlink must not stall; invalid buffers need not be deallocated.

Requirement.text: Each failure event shall be limited to five emissions per 60-second throttle period per component instance; the period starts at the first emission and the quota is re-armed by the first emission request at or after the period elapses. Buffer returns and ready-for-more status shall continue while an event is suppressed.
Requirement.rationale: Persistent failures must not flood the event stream or stall ownership returns, yet must remain observable while they persist.

Requirement.text: `CfdpManager` shall support CFDP Class 1 (unacknowledged) file transfers
Requirement.rationale: Provides unreliable but low-overhead file transfer for non-critical data where speed is prioritized over guaranteed delivery

Requirement.text: `CfdpManager` shall support CFDP Class 2 (acknowledged) file transfers with automatic retransmission
Requirement.rationale: Ensures reliable file delivery with guaranteed completion even over lossy communication links

Requirement.text: `CfdpManager` shall detect missing file segments using gap tracking and request retransmission via NAK PDUs
Requirement.rationale: Provides the mechanism to recover from lost file data PDUs in Class 2 transfers

Requirement.text: `CfdpManager` shall verify file integrity using CRC checksums and reject files with checksum mismatches
Requirement.rationale: Ensures data corruption is detected and prevents accepting corrupted files

Requirement.text: `CfdpManager` shall support multiple simultaneous file transfers across configurable channels
Requirement.rationale: Allows concurrent file operations to maximize throughput and operational flexibility

Requirement.text: `CfdpManager` shall support directory playback operations to transfer all files from a specified directory
Requirement.rationale: Provides batch file transfer capability for operational efficiency

Requirement.text: `CfdpManager` shall support directory polling operations to automatically detect and transfer new files at configurable intervals
Requirement.rationale: Enables autonomous file downlink without ground intervention

Requirement.text: `CfdpManager` shall enforce configurable ACK and NAK retry limits and abandon transactions that exceed these limits
Requirement.rationale: Prevents infinite retry loops and ensures forward progress when peer becomes unresponsive

Requirement.text: `CfdpManager` shall detect transaction inactivity using configurable timeout values and abandon inactive transactions
Requirement.rationale: Reclaims resources from stalled transactions and prevents resource exhaustion

Requirement.text: `CfdpManager` shall support configurable file archiving to move completed files instead of deletion
Requirement.rationale: Preserves files for audit trails and operational analysis while managing storage

Requirement.text: `CfdpManager` shall support both command-initiated and port-initiated file transfers
Requirement.rationale: Allows both ground operators and onboard components to initiate file transfers

Requirement.text: `CfdpManager` shall support flow control to freeze and resume channel operations
Requirement.rationale: Provides mechanism to temporarily halt file transfers during critical spacecraft operations

Requirement.text: `CfdpManager` shall process malformed or degenerate received PDUs, including zero-length FileData segments, without raising a FATAL assertion
Requirement.rationale: Preserves deployment availability against untrusted link input and prevents a single crafted PDU from terminating the process ([GHSA-mh5x-2m6h-8267](https://github.com/nasa/fprime/security/advisories/GHSA-mh5x-2m6h-8267))

Requirement.text: `CfdpManager` shall skip and report a playback or poll directory entry whose combined source or destination path exceeds `MaxFilePathSize`, continuing with the remaining entries without raising a FATAL assertion
Requirement.rationale: Directory contents and the `PlaybackDirectory` arguments are ground-controlled and must not be able to assert the flight software ([#5890](https://github.com/nasa/fprime/issues/5890))

Requirement.text: `CfdpManager` shall treat an `ack_timer` or `inactivity_timer` of zero as expiring on the first 1 Hz cycle after it is armed, without raising a FATAL assertion
Requirement.rationale: `ChannelConfig` is a ground-settable parameter and must not be able to assert the flight software ([#5890](https://github.com/nasa/fprime/issues/5890))

Requirement.text: The ClearTextDecryptor shall accept an SA index, iv/data buffer, and frame context via the `Svc.Ccsds.CcsdsSdlsDecrypt` interface (guarded `decryptIn`).

The ClearTextDecryptor shall pass an `SdlsStatus.SUCCESS` status forward for every request.

The ClearTextEncryptor shall pass an `SdlsStatus.SUCCESS` status forward for every request.
Upon receiving ownership of a buffer back on `encryptReturnIn`, the ClearTextEncryptor shall pass it upstream via `bufferReturnOut` for deallocation.

The SdlsFileKeyManager shall accept key requests via the `Svc.Ccsds.SdlsKeyInterface` interface (guarded `keyGet`), filling the provided `SdlsKeyBuffer`.
Upon a key request, the SdlsFileKeyManager shall read exactly the configured key length from the configured file into the provided buffer and return `SdlsStatus.SUCCESS`.
The SdlsFileKeyManager shall return `SdlsStatus.KEY_ERROR` and emit a WARNING_HI event on any file error (open error, read error, or short read).
The key file path and key length shall be supplied at runtime via `configure()`; the key length shall be in `(0, MAX_SDLS_KEY_SIZE]`. A key request before configuration shall assert.
The SdlsSaRouter shall accept an SA index and iv/data buffer via its guarded `dataIn` port (mirroring the `CcsdsSdlsEncrypt`/`CcsdsSdlsDecrypt` interfaces).

The SdlsSaRouter shall map the incoming SA index to a downstream port index using a compile-time SA-to-port map: an FPP array of {U16 SA, FwIndexType port index} pairs (`SdlsCfg.SaMap`) defined in configuration.
The SdlsSaRouter shall forward the SA index and buffer out the mapped output port, and shall pass the downstream crypto component's `SdlsStatus` forward alongside the processed data via `dataOut`.
The SdlsSaRouter shall receive returned iv/data buffers from downstream crypto components and pass them upstream via its return output.
Upon receiving an SA index with no map entry, the SdlsSaRouter shall pass an `UNKNOWN_SA` status forward on `dataOut` with the untouched buffer, without forwarding it downstream.

Upon a map entry referencing an out-of-range or unconnected port index, the SdlsSaRouter shall pass an `UNKNOWN_PORT` status forward on `dataOut` with the untouched buffer, without forwarding it downstream.
The downstream port arrays shall share a single dimension set by a constant in the component configuration module; the SA-map array dimension shall be an independent config constant.

Downstream crypto components connected to `saDataOut`/`saDataReturnOut` shall invoke `saDataIn`/`saBufferReturnIn` synchronously on the caller's thread (i.e. be passive with synchronous handlers). Asynchronous (queued or hardware-backed) crypto components must not be connected to these ports without adding external synchronization.

The SdlsSaRouter shall accept a replacement SA-to-port map via `configure()`, applied before any frame is routed, so that the uplink and downlink instances may hold distinct tables as required for simplex security associations (CCSDS 355.0-B-2 §2.3.1.1).

The `Svc::CmdSequencer` component shall read sequence files.
Requirement.rationale: CmdSequencer gets commands from the sequence file.

Requirement.text: The `Svc::CmdSequencer` component shall validate the sequence files with a CRC.
Requirement.rationale: CmdSequencer need to know it has a valid file.

Requirement.text: The `Svc::CmdSequencer` component shall provide a command to validate the sequence file.
Requirement.rationale: Waiting to validate the file only when running it can cause operational issues

Requirement.text: The `Svc::CmdSequencer` component shall cancel the sequence upon receiving a failed command status.
Requirement.rationale: A sequence should not continue if a command fails since subsequent commands may depend on the outcome

Requirement.text: The `Svc::CmdSequencer` component shall provide a command to cancel the existing sequence
Requirement.rationale: Operator should be able to cancel the sequence if it is hung or needs to be stopped.

Requirement.text: The `Svc::CmdSequencer` component shall provide a per-command timeout that restarts for each dispatched command.
Requirement.rationale: Sequencer should quit if a component fails to send a command response

The `Svc::CmdSplitter` component shall accept incoming command buffers.
The `Svc::CmdSplitter` component shall route commands under a configured value to the "local" port.
The `Svc::CmdSplitter` component shall route commands under a configured value to the "remote" port.
The `Svc::CmdSplitter` component shall route commands to the "local" port when an error occurs.
The `Svc::CmdSplitter` component shall forward command status responses.

The ComLogger component shall optionally prefix each logged buffer with a 2-byte (U16) length field
The ComLogger component shall close the current file and open a new one when the configured maximum file size would be exceeded
The ComLogger component shall name log files using the configured prefix and the time of file opening
The ComLogger component shall write a hash (validation) file when closing each log file
The ComLogger component shall provide a command to close the currently open file
The ComLogger component shall report file errors via events
The ComLoggerDp component shall log the contents of Com buffers received on its `comIn` port
The ComLoggerDp component shall have a command to start recording packets, specifying the number of packets per container
The ComLoggerDp component shall have a command to stop recording packets

`Svc::ComQueue` shall queue `Fw::Buffer` and `Fw::ComBuffer` received on incoming ports.
Requirement.rationale: The purpose of the queue is to store messages.

Requirement.text: `Svc::ComQueue` shall output exactly one `Fw::Buffer` (wrapping the queued data units) on a received `Fw::Success::SUCCESS` signal. `Fw::Success::SUCCESS` is valid at start-up (to initiate flow), in response to a sent message, or after a previous `Fw::Success::FAILURE` (to indicate recovery).
Requirement.rationale: `Svc::ComQueue` obeys the [communication adapter interface protocol](../../../docs/reference/communication-adapter-interface.md#communication-queue-protocol).

Requirement.text: `Svc::ComQueue` shall pause sending on `Fw::Success::FAILURE` and resume on the next `Fw::Success::SUCCESS` signal.
Requirement.rationale: `Svc::ComQueue` should not send to a failing communication adapter.

Requirement.text: `Svc::ComQueue` shall have a configurable number of `Fw::Com` and `Fw::Buffer` input ports.
Requirement.rationale: `Svc::ComQueue` should be adaptable for a number of projects.

Requirement.text: `Svc::ComQueue` shall select and send the next priority `Fw::Buffer` and `Fw::ComBuffer` message in response to `Fw::Success::SUCCESS`.
Requirement.rationale: `Svc::ComQueue` obeys the [communication adapter interface protocol](../../../docs/reference/communication-adapter-interface.md#communication-queue-protocol).

Requirement.text: `Svc::ComQueue` shall periodically telemeter the number of queued messages per-port in response to a `run` port invocation.
Requirement.rationale: `Svc::ComQueue` should provide useful telemetry.

Requirement.text: `Svc::ComQueue` shall emit a queue overflow event for a given port when the configured depth is exceeded. Messages shall be discarded.
Requirement.rationale: `Svc::ComQueue` needs to indicate off-nominal events.

Requirement.text: `Svc::ComQueue` shall implement a round robin approach to balance between ports of the same priority.
Requirement.rationale: Allows projects to balance between a set of queues of similar priority.

Requirement.text: `Svc::ComQueue` shall keep track and throttle queue overflow events per port.
Requirement.rationale: Prevents a flood of queue overflow events.

Requirement.text: `Svc::ComQueue` shall return ownership of incoming buffers once they have been enqueued.
Requirement.rationale: Memory management

Requirement.text: `Svc::ComQueue` shall provide a command to flush queued items.
Requirement.rationale: Queue management

Requirement.text: `Svc::ComQueue` shall accept a configured depth of 0 for a port, allocating no storage for that queue and treating any message received on that port as an overflow.
Requirement.rationale: Deployments may leave a port unused (e.g. no file downlink) without allocating memory or crashing.

Requirement.text: `Svc::ComQueue` shall report cumulative, per-port message drops caused by async ingress and managed queue overflow separately, including both overflow policies and disabled queues.
Requirement.rationale: Provide observability without generating additional messages during ingress saturation.

Requirement.text: `Svc::ComRetry` shall accept incoming downlink data as `Fw::Buffer` and pass them to an `Svc.ComDataWithContext` port

Requirement.text: `Svc::ComRetry` shall store `Fw::Buffer` and its context on receiving buffer ownership through `dataReturnIn`

Requirement.text: `Svc::ComRetry` shall pause delivery on receiving `Fw::Success::FAILURE`
Requirement.rationale: `Svc::ComRetry` should not send to a failing communication adapter.

Requirement.text: `Svc::ComRetry` shall resend `Fw::Buffer` on receiving `Fw::Success::SUCCESS` after prior failure if retries are available

Requirement.text: `Svc::ComRetry` shall pass through the initial start-up `Fw::Success::SUCCESS` and any non-data statuses upstream when no buffer is pending
Requirement.rationale: The initial SUCCESS must reach `Svc::ComQueue` to initiate data flow per the [Communication Queue Protocol](../../../docs/reference/communication-adapter-interface.md#communication-queue-protocol)

Requirement.text: The maximum number of retries shall be configurable
Requirement.rationale: The number of retries should be adaptable for projects

Requirement.text: `Svc::ComRetry` shall return buffer ownership to the upstream component on receiving `Fw::Success::SUCCESS` or after all retry attempts fail
Requirement.rationale: Memory management

Requirement.text: `Svc::ComRetry` shall send `ComStatus` upstream on successful delivery or after all retry attempts fail
Requirement.rationale: Status of message delivery must be passed up the stack

Requirement.text: `Svc::ComStub` shall send a `Fw::Success::FAILURE` signal via `comStatusOut` on `Drv::ByteStreamSend` failure
Requirement.rationale: Failed sends must notify any attached `Svc::ComQueue` per the [Communication Adapter Protocol](../../../docs/reference/communication-adapter-interface.md#communication-adapter-protocol)

Requirement.text: `Svc::ComStub` shall retry sending to `Drv::ByteStreamSend` on `Drv::ByteStreamSend` retry
Requirement.rationale: Sends indicating `RETRY` should be retried.

Requirement.text: `Svc::ComStub` shall pass-through `Fw::Buffer` from a  `Drv::ByteStreamRead` on `Drv::ByteStreamSend` success
Requirement.rationale: A Comm interface must receive `Fw::Buffer`s from a driver

Requirement.text: `Svc::ComStub` shall emit exactly one `Fw::Success::SUCCESS` via `comStatusOut` on start-up / driver connection to initiate data flow
Requirement.rationale: Initial SUCCESS is required to start the [Communication Queue Protocol](../../../docs/reference/communication-adapter-interface.md#communication-queue-protocol)

Requirement.text: `Svc::ComStub` shall emit exactly one `Fw::Success::SUCCESS` via `comStatusOut` after a driver reconnection following a previous failure to indicate recovery
Requirement.rationale: Recovery SUCCESS resumes data flow per the [Communication Adapter Protocol](../../../docs/reference/communication-adapter-interface.md#communication-adapter-protocol)

Requirement.text: `DpCatalog` shall read a set of directories and build a catalog of data products.
Requirement.rationale: `DpCatalog` needs to know at least one directory where data products reside

Requirement.text: `DpCatalog` shall sort data products first based on the internally recorded priority where the highest priority is represented by the lowest number.
Requirement.rationale: `DpCatalog` needs to downlink highest priority items first

Requirement.text: `DpCatalog` shall sort data products second based on the internally recorded time with oldest products as higher priority.
Requirement.rationale: `DpCatalog` needs to downlink oldest items first

Requirement.text: `DpCatalog` shall sort data products third based on the internally recorded product ID with the lowest as higher priority.
Requirement.rationale: `DpCatalog` needs to resolve case where priority and time match

Requirement.text: `DpCatalog` shall update the data product metadata once download is complete
Requirement.rationale: `DpCatalog` needs to track completion status to avoid duplicate downloads

Requirement.text: `DpCatalog` shall implement a command and port to build the catalog.
Requirement.rationale: `DpCatalog` should consume the resources to build the catalog only when needed

Requirement.text: `DpCatalog` shall implement a command and port to start downloading the catalog.
Requirement.rationale: `DpCatalog` downloads should be timed for when communications are ready, and not consume comm window time building

Requirement.text: `DpCatalog` shall have filters for the download based on container ID, priority, and data size limit.
Requirement.rationale: `DpCatalog` downloads should be tunable for available bandwidth and container metadata

Requirement.text: `DpCatalog` shall implement a way to insert newly-generated data products into the catalog after the catalog is built
Requirement.rationale: `DpCatalog` should notice new products and not require a rebuild of the catalog

Requirement.text: `DpCatalog` shall implement commands to modify the priority of existing data products
Requirement.rationale: Operators made change the priority to lower or raise priorities due to troubleshooting, etc

Requirement.text: `DpCatalog` shall implement commands to delete data products
Requirement.rationale: Ground tools can use DpManager commands to automatically delete DPs

Requirement.text: `DpCatalog` shall implement a catalog data product that is a listing of existing data products and their metadata
Requirement.rationale: Allow operators to know what products exist

Requirement.text: `DpCatalog` shall have filters for the catalog data product for priority, container ID, and time range
Requirement.rationale: Allow operators to know what products exist

Requirement.text: `DpCatalog` shall implement a `START_XMIT_CATALOG_WITH_PRIORITY` command that accepts an inclusive start and end priority and transmits only the pending data products whose priority is within that range, in priority order; `START_XMIT_CATALOG` shall transmit the whole catalog with an unchanged argument list
Requirement.rationale: Operations tune which priority levels are downlinked during a pass without breaking existing sequences

Requirement.text: `START_XMIT_CATALOG_WITH_PRIORITY` shall reject a range whose start priority exceeds its end priority with a `VALIDATION_ERROR` command response and a warning event, leaving the catalog and transmit state unchanged
Requirement.rationale: Invalid ground input must fail visibly and safely

Requirement.text: Data products outside the requested priority range shall remain pending in the catalog, available to a later transmit command, without any change to the catalog data structures or the state file format
Requirement.rationale: The range is a transmit filter, not a deletion; existing state files stay compatible

Requirement.text: `DpCatalog` shall implement a command that sets the transmit priority of one data product, identified by container ID and time tag, so that it is transmitted in the order given by the new priority
Requirement.rationale: Operators may raise or lower the priority of a product to debug an issue or prioritize data (#5860); implements SVC-DPCAT-010

Requirement.text: `DpCatalog` shall reject a priority change for a data product that is not in the catalog with an event and a failed command response
Requirement.rationale: Operators need to know the product was not affected

Requirement.text: `DpCatalog` shall apply a priority change made during catalog transmission to the transmit order of the products not yet sent without disturbing the send in flight
Requirement.rationale: Operators change priorities during a pass; the transmit must not be corrupted

Requirement.text: `DpCatalog` shall treat a priority change to the current priority as a no-op that reports the unchanged priority and succeeds
Requirement.rationale: Idempotent command for sequences

Requirement.text: `DpCatalog` shall record a priority change in the state file, when one is configured, so that it is kept across catalog rebuilds and restarts, without modifying the data product file or the state file format
Requirement.rationale: The change outlives a restart before the pass (#5860); the file is mission data and existing state files stay readable

Requirement.text: `DpCatalog` shall report with an event, and fail the command, a priority change that cannot be recorded in the configured state file
Requirement.rationale: Operators know when the change will not survive a restart

Requirement.text: `DpCatalog` shall implement a command that deletes one data product, identified by container ID and time tag, removing its file, its catalog entry and its record in the state file, when one is configured
Requirement.rationale: Operators and ground tools reclaim storage from products that are transmitted or no longer wanted (SVC-DPCAT-011)

Requirement.text: `DpCatalog` shall refuse to delete the data product being transmitted, and shall reject with an event and a failed command response a product that it does not know
Requirement.rationale: The send in flight is never preempted; operators need to know when nothing was deleted

Requirement.text: `DpCatalog` shall implement a command that reschedules one transmitted data product, identified by container ID and time tag, for downlink at its header priority, resetting its transmitted state in memory and in the state file, when one is configured
Requirement.rationale: Data products may be corrupted in transit or lost on the ground and must be downlinked again (#6284)

Requirement.text: `DpCatalog` shall reject a retransmit request with an event naming the reason and a failed command response when the catalog is not built, the product is being transmitted or is pending, no file of the product exists in a managed directory, or the file cannot be cataloged
Requirement.rationale: The operator must learn why nothing was rescheduled; a pending or in-flight product is sent anyway

Requirement.text: A product rescheduled for retransmission shall be downlinked as a product inserted at runtime is: by the transmission in progress, by resuming a finished or stopped transmission under `remainActive`, or by the next transmit command
Requirement.rationale: Retransmission reuses the existing downlink scheduling rather than adding a second path

Requirement.text: `DpCatalog` shall skip, with an event, a state file record whose directory index is not in the configured directory list
Requirement.rationale: The directory list can change across a restart, and a corrupt record must not index past the directory list

Requirement.text: `Svc::DpCompressProc` shall return the passed `Fw::Buffer` as either a valid compressed data product or the original uncompressed data product. However the data checksum for the container does not need to be valid in the returned product
`Svc::DpCompressProc` shall not allocate additional memory when processing the container. This does not apply to any downstream compressor which is allow to allocate memory
`Svc::DpCompressProc` shall support a user modifiable chunking size
`Svc::DpManager` shall provide an array of ports for synchronously requesting and receiving data product buffers.
Requirement.rationale: This capability supports the `product` `get` port in the auto-generated code for components that define data products.

Requirement.text: `Svc::DpManager` shall provide arrays of ports for receiving and asynchronously responding to requests for data product buffers.
Requirement.rationale: This capability supports the `product` `request` and `product` `recv` ports in the auto-generated code for components that define data products.

Requirement.text: `Svc::DpManager` shall receive data product buffers and forward them for further processing.
Requirement.rationale: This requirement provides a pass-through capability for sending data product buffers to downstream components. `Svc::DpManager` receives data product input on a port of type  `Fw::DpSend`. This input consists of a container ID and an `Fw::Buffer` _B_. `Svc::DpManager` sends _B_ on a port of type `Fw::BufferSend`. This port type is used by the standard F Prime components for managing and logging data, e.g., `Svc::BufferAccumulator`, `Svc::DpWriter`.

Requirement.text: `Svc::DpManager` shall provide telemetry that reports the number of successful allocations, the number of failed allocations, and the volume of data handled.
Requirement.rationale: This requirement establishes the telemetry interface for the component.

Requirement.text: `Svc::DpWriter` shall provide an array of ports for receiving `Fw::Buffer` objects pointing to filled data product containers.
Requirement.rationale: The purpose of `DpWriter` is to write the data products to disk. The array permits the fusion of multiple logical writer components with separate routing paths into a single component. This fusion increases resource efficiency (it requires fewer component instances and threads), but it restricts concurrency by forcing sequential execution of all routing paths on the same thread. The component allows developers to manage this tradeoff.

Requirement.text: `Svc::DpWriter` shall provide an array of ports for sending `Fw::Buffer` objects for processing.
Requirement.rationale: This requirement supports downstream processing of the data in the buffer.

Requirement.text: On receiving a data product container _C_, `Svc::DpWriter` shall use the processing type field of the header of _C_ to select zero or more processing ports to invoke, in port order.
Requirement.rationale: The processing type field is a bit mask. A one in bit `2^n` in the bit mask selects port index `n`.

Requirement.text: On receiving an `Fw::Buffer` _B_, and after performing any requested processing on _B_, `Svc::DpWriter` shall write _B_ to disk.
Requirement.rationale: The purpose of `DpWriter` is to write data products to the disk.

Requirement.text: `Svc::DpWriter` shall provide an array of ports for notifying other components that data products have been written. A notification shall use the same routing port index as the corresponding input buffer.
Requirement.rationale: The notification output allows `Svc::DpCatalog` or a similar component to update a data product catalog in real time. It is possible to notify a single instance of `Svc::DpCatalog` of all outputs, by connecting all the output ports of `Svc::DpWriter` to that component. It is also possible to notify different components via the different output ports. The array preserves symmetry across the port behaviors of this component (input, buffer return, and notification).

Requirement.text: `Svc::DpWriter` shall provide telemetry that reports the number of buffers received, the number of data products written, the number of bytes written, the number of failed writes, and the number of errors.
Requirement.rationale: This requirement establishes the telemetry interface for the component.

Requirement.text: On receiving an `Fw::Buffer` _B_, and after performing any requested processing on _B_, `Svc::DpWriter` shall re-parse the container header and shrink the size of the product.
Requirement.rationale: Allows processing interfaces to compress data products and communicate that compressed state back to `Svc::DpWriter`.

Requirement.text: `Svc::DpWriter` shall return each valid received buffer on the `deallocBufferSendOut` port whose index matches the `bufferSendIn` port that received it.
Requirement.rationale: Matching send and return paths allows a `DpWriter` instance to route buffers back toward the correct allocator.

Requirement.text: `Svc::DpZLibCompressor` shall attempt to compress incoming data chunks per the protocol defined by DpCompressProc
`Svc::DpZLibCompressor` shall either return `Svc::CompressionAlgorithm::UNCOMPRESSED` or `Svc::CompressionAlgorithm::ZLIB_DEFLATE` from the compressChunk input port
The `Svc::EventManager` component shall receive events and compose them into downlink packets.
The `Svc::EventManager` component shall have commands to filter events based on event severity.
The `Svc::EventManager` component shall have commands to filter events based on the event ID.
The `Svc::EventManager` component shall call the `FatalAnnounce` port when a FATAL event is received

The `Svc::FatalHandler` component shall shut down the Unix process

File dispatcher will provide a way to dispatch files to other components
Requirement.rationale: Need to have a way to supply a file name for a newly transferred file

Requirement.text: File dispatcher will provide user configuration to map file types to output ports
Requirement.rationale: Projects will want to customize the dispatching types

Requirement.text: File dispatcher will dispatch to specified output ports based on the supplied table
Requirement.rationale: Projects will want to connect the dispatch types to components for processing new files

Requirement.text: `FileDownlink` shall queue up a list of files to downlink
Requirement.rationale: The requirement provides the ability to simultaneously queue up multiple files for downlink from different sources

Requirement.text: `FileDownlink` shall read a file from non-volatile storage, partition the file into packets, and send out the packets.
Requirement.rationale: This requirement provides the capability to downlink files from the spacecraft.

Requirement.text: `FileDownlink` shall wait for a cooldown after completing a file downlink before starting another file downlink
Requirement.rationale: Allows a saturated link to process a backlog that may have built up during a file downlink

Requirement.text: `FileDownlink` shall issue a warning if a file with zero size is encountered
Requirement.rationale: Ensures that operators are aware of invalid file sizes

Requirement.text: `FileUplink` shall receive file packets, assemble them into files, and store the files in the on-board non-volatile storage.
Requirement.rationale: This requirement provides the capability to uplink files to the spacecraft.

Requirement.text: `FileUplink` shall announce the completion of uplinked files.
Requirement.rationale: This requirement provides the capability to inform other components of newly uplinked files

Requirement.text: `Svc::FprimeDeframer` shall extract the payload field from input buffers that represent a valid F Prime frame as specified by the [F Prime Protocol](../../FprimeProtocol/docs/sdd.md)
Requirement.rationale: Deframe valid frames and extract payload

Requirement.text: `Svc::FprimeDeframer` shall return ownership of input buffers that are not a valid F Prime frame as specified by the [F Prime Protocol](../../FprimeProtocol/docs/sdd.md)
Requirement.rationale: Drop invalid frames

Requirement.text: `Svc::FprimeFramer` shall accept data buffers (packets) stored in `Fw::Buffer` through its `dataIn` input port
`Svc::FprimeFramer` shall emit one F Prime frame on its `dataOut` output port for each packet received on `dataIn` input port
`Svc::FprimeFramer` shall emit F Prime frames that conforms to the [F´ frame specification](../../FprimeProtocol/docs/sdd.md)

`Svc::FprimeFramer` shall pass through all `Fw.SuccessCondition` received on `comStatusIn` to `comStatusOut`, including the initial start-up `Fw::Success::SUCCESS`, per-message statuses, and any recovery `Fw::Success::SUCCESS` after a `Fw::Success::FAILURE`, per the [Framer Status Protocol](../../../docs/reference/communication-adapter-interface.md#framer-status-protocol)

`Svc::FprimeRouter` shall route packets based on their packet type as indicated by the packet header
Requirement.rationale: Routing mechanism of the F´ comms protocol

Requirement.text: `Svc::FprimeRouter` shall route packets of type `Fw::ComPacketType::FW_PACKET_COMMAND` to the `commandOut` output port.
Requirement.rationale: Routing command packets

Requirement.text: `Svc::FprimeRouter` shall route packets of type `Fw::ComPacketType::FW_PACKET_FILE` to the `fileOut` output port.
Requirement.rationale: Routing file packets

Requirement.text: `Svc::FprimeRouter` shall route data that is neither `Fw::ComPacketType::FW_PACKET_COMMAND` nor `Fw::ComPacketType::FW_PACKET_FILE` to the `unknownDataOut` output port.
Requirement.rationale: Allows for projects to provide custom routing for additional (project-specific) uplink data types

Requirement.text: `Svc::FprimeRouter` shall emit warning events if serialization errors occur during processing of incoming packets
Requirement.rationale: Aid in diagnosing uplink issues

Requirement.text: `Svc::FprimeRouter` shall pass through buffers for `FW_PACKET_FILE` and unknown packet types without copying, and defer returning them to the deframer until they are returned via `fileBufferReturnIn`
Requirement.rationale: Efficient memory management

Requirement.text: `Svc::FprimeRouter` shall return ownership of all buffers received on `dataIn` through `dataReturnOut`
Requirement.rationale: Memory management

Requirement.text: `Svc::FprimeRouter` shall preserve the `ComCfg::FrameContext` received on `dataIn` and restore it on the corresponding `dataReturnOut`, including across the `fileOut`/`unknownDataOut` → `fileBufferReturnIn` round-trip
Requirement.rationale: Allows a shared router to return buffers to the correct originating uplink path (e.g. by `vcId`)

Requirement.text: `Svc::FprimeRouter` shall emit a warning event and return the buffer with an empty context when the buffer-to-context table is full on hand-off, or when a returned buffer is not found in the table
Requirement.rationale: Graceful degradation without loss of buffer ownership

Requirement.text: `Svc::FrameAccumulator` shall accumulate a sequence of byte buffers until a full frame is received
Requirement.rationale: FrameAccumulator is designed to re-assemble frames from sequence of bytes

Requirement.text: `Svc::FrameAccumulator` shall detect once the accumulated buffers form a full frame and emit said frame
Requirement.rationale: Pass frames to other parts of the system

Requirement.text: `Svc::FrameAccumulator` shall accept byte buffers containing frames that are not aligned on a buffer boundary.
Requirement.rationale: For flexibility, we do not require that the frames be aligned on a buffer boundary.

Requirement.text: `Svc::FrameAccumulator` shall accept byte buffers containing frames that span one or more buffers.
Requirement.rationale: For flexibility, we do not require each frame to fit in a single buffer.

`Svc::TimeConverter` shall store offsets between pairs of time bases, keyed by the pair in a canonical order so that one entry serves both directions.

`Svc::TimeConverter` shall store at most a compile-time configurable number of offset entries.
`Svc::TimeConverter` shall emit a warning event and discard the update when an offset update would exceed the configured table capacity.

`Svc::TimeConverter` shall convert a supplied time to a requested time base by applying the stored offset for that pair, negating the stored offset when the conversion runs opposite to the stored direction, and shall report success.
`Svc::TimeConverter` shall preserve the time context of the input time in the converted output time.
`Svc::TimeConverter` shall report success without altering the value when the source and requested time bases are identical.
`Svc::TimeConverter` shall report `UNKNOWN_TIMEBASE`, emit a throttled warning event, and leave the output unmodified when no offset is stored for the requested pair.
`Svc::TimeConverter` shall report `INVALID_TIME`, emit a throttled warning event, and leave the output unmodified when the conversion would produce a time not representable as an `Fw::Time`.

`Svc::TimeConverter` shall accept a command that sets the offset for a pair of time bases, with the same effect as an offset update received over the port, shall report the stored offset as an event, and shall reject the command with a warning event when an argument is rejected.
`Svc::TimeConverter` shall accept a command that discards every stored offset and reports the number discarded as an event.

`Svc::TimeConverter` shall accept a command that reports the offset stored for a single pair of time bases as an event, and shall reject the command with a warning event when no offset is stored for that pair or when both ends of the pair are the same time base.
`Svc::TimeConverter` shall accept a command that reports every stored offset as events, and shall emit an event reporting an empty table when no offsets are stored.
`Svc::TimeConverter` shall perform conversions and offset updates without dynamic memory allocation and in bounded time.

`Svc::TimeConverter` shall reject a time base that denotes no clock, `TB_NONE` or `TB_DONT_CARE`, wherever it is supplied as an end of a pair, and shall emit a throttled high-severity warning event naming it.

Requirement.text: The sequencer shall support loading and validating WebAssembly modules.
Requirement.rationale: Sequences are distributed as WebAssembly binaries; a module must be decoded and validated before execution so a malformed or untrusted binary cannot corrupt the host.

Requirement.text: The sequencer shall support loading multiple named modules so that the exports of one module may be referenced by another.
Requirement.rationale: Larger sequences are composed from reusable library modules; naming lets inter-module imports and exports resolve within a single store.

Requirement.text: The sequencer shall allocate its module store for a fixed, configured capacity and shall reset it on a failed load.
Requirement.rationale: Flight software forbids heap fragmentation; a fixed-capacity store with a full reset on failure keeps allocation deterministic and returns to a known-good state.

Requirement.text: The sequencer shall resolve sequence file paths relative to a configurable base directory.
Requirement.rationale: Onboard sequence storage varies by deployment; a parameterized base directory avoids hard-coding filesystem layout into the flight software.

Requirement.text: The sequencer shall support running sequences with arguments.
Requirement.rationale: Passing arguments at dispatch time lets a single sequence binary be parameterized, so operators can reuse one module across scenarios instead of rebuilding per run.

Requirement.text: The sequencer shall support invoking a previously loaded module's entry point on demand.
Requirement.rationale: Decoupling load from invoke lets a module be validated and staged ahead of time, then executed without re-reading the file.

Requirement.text: The sequencer shall support both blocking and non-blocking sequence execution.
Requirement.rationale: Blocking lets a controlling sequence or operator wait for completion; non-blocking allows fire-and-forget dispatch. Both are needed depending on the caller's intent.

Requirement.text: The sequencer shall bound the number of interpreter instructions executed per cycle.
Requirement.rationale: Fuelling the interpreter keeps a long-running or malicious guest from starving the component thread and preserves responsiveness to pause and cancellation.

Requirement.text: The sequencer shall support pausing a running sequence before the next directive and later resuming it.
Requirement.rationale: Operators need to halt a sequence at a safe point for inspection or intervention and resume it without restarting from the beginning.

Requirement.text: The sequencer shall support cancelling a loading, ready, or running sequence and returning to the idle state.
Requirement.rationale: An operator must be able to abort a misbehaving or unneeded sequence at any point and clear the store to a known-good idle state.

Requirement.text: The sequencer shall fail a sequence whose current blocking host function does not complete within a configurable timeout.
Requirement.rationale: A command or serial reply that never arrives would block the sequencer indefinitely; a per-host-function timeout bounds the wait and fails the sequence safely.

Requirement.text: The sequencer shall let a sequence read the current spacecraft time, telemetry channel values, and parameter values.
Requirement.rationale: Time-aware and conditional sequences must branch on the host's authoritative time, live telemetry, and configured parameters rather than guest-local state.

Requirement.text: The sequencer shall support dispatching commands.
Requirement.rationale: Command dispatch is the primary mechanism by which a sequence actuates the spacecraft.

Requirement.text: The sequencer shall let a sequence emit events at the non-reserved F´ severities.
Requirement.rationale: Guest programs need operator-visible logging; restricting to `WARNING_LO`/`HI`, `ACTIVITY_LO`/`HI` and `DIAGNOSTIC` severities prevents untrusted code from triggering the FATAL handler or spoofing command events.

Requirement.text: The sequencer shall let a sequence sleep for a relative or absolute duration.
Requirement.rationale: Sequences must pace their actions against wall-clock time (settling delays, timed maneuvers) without busy-waiting and consuming interpreter fuel.

Requirement.text: The sequencer shall let a sequence support invoking a serial output port at a given index.
Requirement.rationale: General communication with other components (or sequencers) is useful for synchronizing actions or communicating state. Projects can decide how and what capabilities are exposed to sequences.

Requirement.text: The sequencer shall let a sequence read a message from a serial input port, either blocking until one arrives or returning immediately when none is queued.
Requirement.rationale: The inverse of WASM-SEQ-016 is needed to support general communication between other components or sequences. Blocking and non-blocking receives are useful mechanisms to implement event driven and polling workloads.

Requirement.text: The sequencer shall treat a sequence that terminates with a zero return value or a zero exit code as a success, and a non-zero return value, a non-zero exit code, or a panic as a failure.
Requirement.rationale: Guests need a clean way to end execution; treating a zero return or exit(0) as success and any non-zero return value, non-zero exit code, or panic as a failure lets the host report the correct verdict to the awaiting command.

Requirement.text: The sequencer shall validate all host-function arguments from the guest and never fault the host on invalid input, reporting an event and failing or trapping the sequence instead.
Requirement.rationale: Untrusted guest code must never be able to crash the host. This covers oversized/undersized buffers, out-of-range or unconnected serial ports, invalid guest memory pointers, and reserved-severity event requests, all of which are rejected gracefully rather than asserting.

Requirement.text: The sequencer shall report its current state, running sequence name, and most recent trap reason as telemetry.
Requirement.rationale: Operators need continuous visibility into what the sequencer is doing and why a sequence stopped without pulling a full event log.

Requirement.text: The sequencer shall count and report sequences succeeded, failed, and cancelled, and commands dispatched and failed.
Requirement.rationale: Aggregate counters give operators a quick health indicator and let ground trend sequence and command reliability over a mission.

Requirement.text: The sequencer shall let a running sequence grow its linear memory via `memory.grow` in strictly O(1) time complexity. Disallowed growth shall telemetry reason to operator.
Requirement.rationale: Guests that size working buffers at run time need `memory.grow`. Certain kinds of memory growth are O(1) (i.e. increment a counter) while others require O(n) data copy or move (these are not allowed).

Requirement.text: The sequencer shall let an operator read, and write (when mutable), a loaded module's exported globals addressed by module and global name.
Requirement.rationale: Exposing module globals lets ground inspect and adjust sequence state (tuning constants, flags, thresholds) without reloading, and enables coordination through shared globals; type mismatches, immutable targets, and unknown module/global names are rejected without disturbing the store.

Requirement.text: The sequencer shall reject a `RUN`, `LOAD`, or `INVOKE` request that arrives while it is already loading or running a sequence, responding `BUSY` without disturbing the in-progress sequence.
Requirement.rationale: The store and interpreter serve one sequence at a time. Reject overlapping requests with `BUSY` keeps execution deterministic and prevents a late or spurious request from corrupting an in-flight sequence.

Requirement.text: The sequencer shall report the outcome of every port-requested sequence run on `seqDoneOut`.
Requirement.rationale: A caller such as `Svc::SeqDispatcher` reserves a sequencer slot the instant it makes the request and releases it only on a done report, so an unreported outcome retires that sequencer for the rest of the mission.
